messages.subject: Differentially methylated genes
messages.body_plain:
Hi, Altuna,
I have used  methylkit and genomation for DMR analysis and it works very well. I have a question, to identify DMR, I used tileMethylcounts function with specified windowsize and stepsize to define the regions. Then I used the annotateWithGeneParts and getAssociationWithTSS to get their genomic feature to see where the DMR overlaps with specific genes. I am wondering whether it is possible to directly compare the methylation difference on a per-gene basis without defining the window of regions but using the gene length as the window? Is it possible to do that using methylkit and genomation?
Thanks in advance!
Lei

> Please check out this example code:
>
> ```
> library("methylKit")
> library(parallel)
>

>   system.file("extdata", "control1.myCpG.txt", package = "methylKit"),
>   system.file("extdata", "control2.myCpG.txt", package = "methylKit")
> )
>
> sample.ids=list("test1","test2","ctrl1","ctrl2")
>
> treatment = c(1,1, 0,0)
>
> res = methylRawList(
>   treatment = treatment,
>   mcmapply(
>     FUN = methRead,
>     file.list,
>     sample.ids,
>     assembly = "hg18",
>     SIMPLIFY = FALSE,
>     mc.cores = 3
>   )
> )
>
> resDB = methylRawListDB(
>   treatment = treatment,
>   mcmapply(

>     file.list,
>     sample.ids,
>     assembly = "hg18",

David

messages.subject_clean: Need to edit a string in methylDiff object
messages.body_plain:
Hi Caleb,

The difference in chromosome naming conventions is a common problem in bioinformatics, that you are going to encounter many more times in the future ;)
My recommendation would be to either fetch a matching annotation or learn how to modify annotation files to adjust the chromosome naming yourself using the sed command <https://bioinformaticsworkbook.org/Appendix/Unix/unix-basics-4sed.html#gsc.tab=0>. This way you fix the annotation in the beginning and make sure it matches with any downstream output.

Anyways, back to your problem.

The dplyr functions are expecting a `data.frame` to do their job and while a methylDiff is derived from a data.frame it is not directly supported.

If you want to use tidyverse functions on methylKit objects I suggest you first convert the objects to data.frame using `getData`:
```myDiff25p %>% getData %>%  mutate(chr = str_replace(chr, 'M821.3ch*', 'chr'))```

However, since a methylDiff is derived from a data.frame you may also just directly change the chromosome column:
```myDiff25p$chr <- str_replace(myDiff25p$chr, 'M821.3ch*', 'chr')```

Best,
Alex
